subject: Re: Mutual Action Plan — Redwood Inference & Acme Corp
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Tom Li <tom.li@acme.com>, Sophie Hayes <sophie.hayes@acme.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Mar 2027 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap & proposed Mutual Action Plan (MAP) — Redwood + Acme

Tom & Sophie — great speaking with you today. Thanks for walking through Acme's current inference bottlenecks and the decision process. Below is a concise recap, open questions, and the proposed MAP with milestones and owners. I attached a working MAP spreadsheet (.xlsx) and a short architecture diagram.

Quick recap of pain & goals
- Pain: high per-token cost and inconsistent latency on peak traffic (esp. recommendation API), KV cache misses across sessions, and no current fallback path for latency spikes.
- Business goals: reduce inference TCO by 30% for recommendation flows, achieve p95 latency <= 250ms for interactive endpoints, and have a tested disaster/fallback plan before Q3 pilot.

Key stakeholders (as called out on the call)
- Tom Li — CTO (final technical approval)
- Sophie Hayes — Head of Product (product/metrics owner)
- Procurement (procurement@acme.com) — contracting and PO
- Internal: Marissa Cole (AE), Vivek Kulkarni (SE), Rishi Malhotra (Solutions Engineer), Monica Patel (CS)

Proposed Mutual Action Plan (draft milestones & dates)
1) Technical scoping & access (Mar 3) — SE trial account + sample traffic (Vivek / Rishi)
2) Pilot deployment (Mar 10–Mar 24) — run recommendation model on dedicated pool, measure p50/p95/p99 and cost per 1k tokens (Acme + Redwood)
3) Eval & quality/signoff (Mar 25–Mar 29) — product & ML evaluate outputs vs baseline (Sophie / Tom)
4) Procurement & legal (Mar 25–Apr 7) — finalize SOW and PO (Procurement / Marissa)
5) Production rollout readiness (Apr 14) — autoscale policies, canary, and fallback configured (Engineering teams)

Open questions / items I need from you
- Sample traffic: can you share a 24–72 hour anonymized sample of recommendation requests (headers + payload sizes)?
- Success metric thresholds: confirm the target p95 (we noted 250ms, confirm) and acceptable quality delta vs your baseline model.
- Procurement contact and preferred contracting terms for a 12-month reserved capacity pilot.

Next steps
- Vivek will reach out to schedule an architecture deep-dive (30–45m) this week.
- I'll share the MAP spreadsheet (attached) and a simple test checklist — please review and drop comments in the Drive link.

Attachments: Acme-MAP-20270301.xlsx (MAP draft), redwood-arch-diagram.pdf (high-level)

Thanks — looking forward to getting the pilot running.
—
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | (415) 555-0123
https://redwood.com

From: Tom Li <tom.li@acme.com>

Subject: Re: Post-call recap & proposed Mutual Action Plan (MAP) — Redwood + Acme

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the clear summary. Confirming the high-level items below:

- We agree with the milestones and timeline; March 10 pilot start date works on our side.
- Target p95 = 250ms for recommendation endpoint; product is ok with up to a 2% quality delta vs baseline during pilot.
- Procurement: procurement@acme.com (Kate Morales is the lead; I CC'd the procurement alias). They typically require a SOW + PO; we can do a standard 60-day net payment term.

Open items from our side:
- We will provide an anonymized 48-hour sample of recommendation traffic by EOD Wed (Mar 3).
- We'll need SE notes on expected telemetry integration (what metrics to collect).

Please add Kate (procurement@acme.com) to the MAP doc and share the Drive link to comments. Vivek — can you propose 2 slots for the architecture deep-dive this week?

Tom
Tom Li | CTO, Acme Corp
